purpose: tinycbor is a low-overhead C library for parsing CBOR streams.

functions.cbor_value_is_valid: `cbor_value_is_valid()` is a simple guard for `CborValue` handles. Use it to check whether a pointer is non-NULL and the value isn’t `CborInvalidType`. It returns `true` only for valid values; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_next_byte: Returns the iterator’s current source pointer (`it->source.ptr`), i.e. the next byte to be read. Use it to inspect where parsing will continue. It does no validation and simply returns the stored pointer.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_map:
Creates a CBOR map container encoder. Use it with a parent encoder and child `mapEncoder`, passing the entry count or `CborIndefiniteLength`. Returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if length is too large; otherwise delegates to container setup.
This crash is due to API misuse upstream: call cbor_encoder_create_map only on a CborEncoder that was initialized with valid, library-defined flags via cbor_encoder_init. Do not pass arbitrary fuzzed bits as the flags argument. Use 0 or documented CborEncoder* flags only, and if using any mode that requires a writer callback/streaming encoder state, initialize the encoder through the corresponding supported setup so the internal union field matches the selected mode. Also check the returned CborError before continuing to use the child encoder.
functions.cbor_value_is_simple_type: `cbor_value_is_simple_type()` checks whether a `CborValue` currently represents a CBOR simple type. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborSimpleType`, otherwise `false`. Use it to test the item kind before reading it as a simple value.
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk: Returns the next chunk of a CBOR string. Pass a `CborValue`; it copies it to `next` (or a temp if `next==NULL`) and calls `get_string_chunk`. Use it to iterate chunked strings; `bufferptr/len` receive the chunk.
functions.cbor_value_leave_container:
Leaves a container after iterating it. Use with `recursed` as the saved iterator state from entering the container; it must be `CborInvalidType`. It copies the end position back, skips the break byte for unknown-length containers, then prepares `it` for the next item.
Only call cbor_value_leave_container() after the iterator returned by cbor_value_enter_container() has reached the end of the container, i.e. recursed->type == CborInvalidType (typically after advancing until cbor_value_at_end(&recursed) is true without error). If cbor_value_advance(&recursed) returns an error while iterating, do not unconditionally call cbor_value_leave_container(); instead propagate/handle the error and abandon that container path.
functions.cbor_encode_floating_point: Encodes a CBOR floating-point item (half/float/double) from raw bits. Pass `fpType` as `CborHalfFloatType`, `CborFloatType`, or `CborDoubleType`, and `value` pointing to a `uint16_t/uint32_t/uint64_t` bit pattern. It writes the type byte + payload; invalid `fpType` is asserted.
functions.cbor_value_get_float:
`cbor_value_get_float` extracts a CBOR float from a `CborValue` into `float`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_float(value)` is true; it asserts that and that the stored integer bits fit the float path. It decodes the raw bits and copies them into `result`, returning `CborNoError`.
Misuse: call this only on a CborValue obtained from normal parsing, after confirming cbor_value_is_float(value) is true, and after ensuring the input buffer is a complete CBOR item. Do not manually set value->type or value->flags. Initialize a CborParser with cbor_parser_init(), advance to the target item using the public iterator APIs, and then invoke cbor_value_get_float() on that parser-produced value.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse. Only call cbor_value_get_float() on a CborValue produced by tinycbor parsing APIs (for example after cbor_parser_init and normal iterator traversal), not on a manually fabricated CborValue. Before calling, ensure cbor_value_is_float(value) is true and preserve the parser-populated internal fields and flags; do not zero or invent value->flags, extra, remaining, source, or parser state. If constructing tests, generate valid CBOR bytes for a float and let tinycbor parse them, then call cbor_value_get_float() on the resulting iterator.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container: Closes a container encoder and syncs parent buffer state to the child. Use after finishing arrays/maps. For unknown-length containers it appends the CBOR break byte. For fixed-length containers it checks item count: too many/too few items errors; OOM if no space for finalization.
functions.cbor_value_get_int: Returns a CBOR integer as `int`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true. It extracts the stored unsigned magnitude, then negates as CBOR negative integer (`-n-1`) if needed. Always returns `CborNoError` here.
functions.cbor_value_get_map_length: Gets a map’s item count. Use only on a map `CborValue`; it asserts that type. If length is indefinite, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. On success writes `*length`; if it won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions.cbor_encode_text_string: Encodes a CBOR text string into the given `encoder`. Pass the UTF-8 bytes in `string` and their byte `length`; it writes a text-string item of that exact length. Returns the `CborError` from `encode_string` (e.g. buffer/encoder errors).
functions.cbor_encode_undefined: Encodes the CBOR `undefined` simple value. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*`; it just forwards to `cbor_encode_simple_value(..., CborUndefinedType & 0x1f)`. Returns that function’s `CborError` result.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64_checked: `cbor_value_get_int64_checked` safely reads a CBOR integer into `int64_t`. Use it only after confirming `cbor_value_is_integer(value)`. It returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the unsigned CBOR value exceeds `INT64_MAX`; otherwise it stores the signed result, handling negative CBOR integers as `-v-1`.
functions.cbor_error_string: Returns a human-readable message for a `CborError`. Use it to report/diagnose errors, not to change control flow. `CborNoError` gives `""`; known codes map to specific strings; unknown/unhandled codes return `"unknown error"`.
functions.cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer: Checks whether a `CborValue` is an integer and not marked negative. Use it to test for CBOR unsigned integers before reading as a non-negative number. Returns true only for positive/zero integer items; false for negatives and non-integers.
functions.cbor_value_advance_fixed:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator by one item for fixed-size CBOR types only. Use it after verifying `it->type` is fixed. If `remaining==0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it calls the internal advance logic.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Only call cbor_value_advance_fixed() when the iterator is positioned on a valid fixed-width CBOR item and previous parsing operations succeeded. Before calling it, check that the current type is not CborInvalidType, that the item is a fixed type, and that the iterator is not at end. Most importantly, do not ignore CborError returns from cbor_value_get_int64, cbor_value_get_double, cbor_value_get_tag, cbor_value_enter_container, or any internal decode helper; if any of these fail, stop processing that iterator instead of advancing it. For non-fixed or uncertain items, prefer cbor_value_advance() or branch on cbor_value_get_type() first.
functions.cbor_value_get_int_checked: `cbor_value_get_int_checked` safely reads a CBOR integer into `int`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true. It returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the CBOR value can’t fit in `int`; otherwise `CborNoError` and stores the result in `*result`.
functions.cbor_encode_boolean: Encodes a CBOR boolean (`false`/`true`) into the given `CborEncoder`. Pass the encoder and a `bool`; it maps to CBOR simple values 20/21 via `cbor_encode_simple_value`. Returns the underlying `CborError`.
functions._cbor_encoder_get_buffer_pointer: Returns the encoder’s current write pointer (`encoder->data.ptr`). Use it to inspect or continue writing at the current buffer position. It doesn’t advance, validate, or modify state; it just returns the internal buffer pointer.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance: Pretty-prints the CBOR item at `*value` to `out` and advances `*value` past it. Use it when iterating through a CBOR stream/item sequence. It just forwards to `cbor_value_to_pretty_stream(..., CborPrettyDefaultFlags)`, so behavior/error handling match that helper.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty: Prints a CBOR value in human-readable form to `FILE *out`. Use it with a valid `CborValue*`; it copies the value first, so the original isn’t advanced. Returns the pretty-printer’s `CborError` from the copy-based traversal.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size:
Returns the current string chunk length while iterating a chunked CBOR string. Use only when `value` is in string-chunk iteration mode; otherwise the assert fires. It forwards to `_cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size` and returns its `CborError`.
Call this API only on a CborValue that is already positioned on a string chunk and has CborIteratorFlag_IteratingStringChunks set. Do not call it on the original iterator for an indefinite-length string. First use the proper chunk-iteration flow (for example, obtain/advance chunk iterators with the string-chunk APIs such as _cbor_value_get_string_chunk), check the returned error code, and only then query the current chunk size. For definite-length strings, use cbor_value_is_length_known() / cbor_value_calculate_string_length() or copy/dup helpers instead of chunk-size iteration APIs.
functions.cbor_encoder_init_writer: Initializes a `CborEncoder` for streaming output via a writer callback. Use it with a callback and token; `end` stores the token, `remaining` starts at 2, and the writer flag is set. If `CBOR_ENCODER_WRITE_FUNCTION` is enabled, the callback is ignored.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_stream: Pretty-prints a `CborValue` to a user-supplied stream callback. Pass the stream function, token, value, and flags. It just forwards to `value_to_pretty(...)` with `CBOR_PARSER_MAX_RECURSIONS`, so behavior/error handling is that helper’s.
functions.cbor_value_finish_string_iteration: `cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()` finalizes an ongoing string/chunk iteration. Call it only after `cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end(value)` is true. It asserts this in debug builds, then delegates to the internal finisher.
functions.cbor_value_skip_tag: `cbor_value_skip_tag` advances a `CborValue` iterator past any leading CBOR tag(s). Use it when you want the tagged item itself, not its tags. It loops over consecutive tags; returns the first error from `cbor_value_advance_fixed`, or `CborNoError` if none remain.
functions.cbor_value_dup_byte_string: Duplicates the current CBOR byte string into a newly allocated `uint8_t*`. Use only when `value` is a byte string; it asserts otherwise. On success, `*buffer` gets the copy, `*buflen` its length, and `next` (if non-NULL) is advanced past the item.
functions.cbor_encode_float_as_half_float: Encodes a `float` as CBOR half-float (16-bit) using `encode_half(value)`, then writes it via `cbor_encode_floating_point`. Use it when you want compact half-precision output. It returns the encoder’s `CborError` result; behavior depends on whether the value can be represented in half-float.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container_checked: `cbor_encoder_close_container_checked()` is a thin wrapper around `cbor_encoder_close_container()`. Use it to close a nested CBOR container with the parent encoder and the child/container encoder. It returns the same `CborError` as the underlying close call.
functions.cbor_value_dup_text_string: Duplicates a CBOR text string into a newly allocated C string. Use it on a `CborValue` that is a text string; it fills `*buffer`, sets `*buflen` to the byte length, and optionally writes the next item to `next`. It asserts if `value` isn’t text.
functions.cbor_encode_half_float: Encodes a CBOR half-precision float (16-bit). Pass a valid `CborEncoder*` and a pointer to the float value storage expected by tinycbor. It just forwards to `cbor_encode_floating_point(..., CborHalfFloatType, ...)`, so errors come from that helper/encoder state.
functions.cbor_value_calculate_string_length: Calculates the decoded length of a CBOR string without copying it. Pass a `CborValue*` for a text/byte string and a `size_t*` out param. It sets `*len` via `_cbor_value_copy_string(..., NULL, len, NULL)`; on error, length may remain `SIZE_MAX`.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_array: Creates a CBOR array container. Call it with a parent encoder, a child encoder, and the item count. It initializes `arrayEncoder` to write array elements; the parent is used to emit the array header. Returns the result of `create_container`, so errors are propagated from that helper.
functions.cbor_value_text_string_equals: Checks whether a CBOR text string equals a NUL-terminated C string. It skips tags, returns `*result=false` if the item isn’t a text string, otherwise compares content chunk-by-chunk via `iterate_memcmp`. Errors from tag skipping/comparison are returned.
functions._cbor_value_copy_string: Copies a CBOR string into a user buffer, using `*buflen` as in/out size. Pass `buffer==NULL` to query required length. On success, `next` gets the following value. If the buffer is too small, it returns `CborErrorOutOfMemory` after copying what fits.
functions.cbor_value_advance:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator to the next item. Use it on a valid, non-invalid iterator. If `remaining == 0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it advances via recursive parser logic and returns the resulting `CborError`.
Yes, this crash is caused by API misuse. Only call cbor_value_advance() on a valid iterator that still points to a current item. Do not call it after recursive traversal has already consumed or invalidated that iterator. In container walks, use one ownership model: either (1) recursively process a child and let that logic advance to the next item, or (2) process only the current item recursively and then advance exactly once in the caller, but never both. Always stop if the iterator reaches end-of-container, if enter/leave container fails, or if the iterator type becomes invalid due to malformed input. In practice, after walk_value(&recursed, ...), avoid an unconditional cbor_value_advance(&recursed); instead ensure the recursive function's contract is clear about whether it leaves recursed on the same item, the next item, or end-of-container.
functions.cbor_value_map_find_value: Finds a text-string key in a CBOR map. Call with a map and C string; `element` is set to the matching value if found. It enters the map, scans key/value pairs, skips tags, compares only text-string keys, and returns `preparse_value(element)` on match; otherwise advances/skips and errors on parse issues.
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float_as_float: Converts a CBOR half-float at `value` into a C `float`. Use it with a valid `CborValue*` and `float* result`. It calls `cbor_value_get_half_float`, asserts that it succeeds, then decodes and stores the value. On success returns `CborNoError`; on failure, the assert fires.
functions.cbor_encode_simple_value: Encodes a CBOR simple value (major type 7) into `encoder`. Use with valid simple values only; if `CBOR_ENCODER_NO_CHECK_USER` is off, values in `[HalfPrecisionFloat..Break]` return `CborErrorIllegalSimpleType`. Otherwise it delegates to `encode_number`.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_extra_bytes_needed: Returns how many extra bytes the encoder still needs to finish the current item. Use it after encoding to check if the output buffer was too small. If `encoder->end` is set, it returns `0`; otherwise it returns `encoder->data.bytes_needed`.
functions.cbor_encode_text_stringz: `cbor_encode_text_stringz()` is a convenience wrapper to encode a NUL-terminated C string as a CBOR text string. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and `const char*`; it measures length via `strlen()`. It returns whatever `cbor_encode_text_string()` returns.
functions.cbor_value_is_undefined: `cbor_value_is_undefined()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` iff `value->type == CborUndefinedType`. Use it on a valid `CborValue` to test whether the current item is CBOR `undefined`; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_map: `cbor_value_is_map()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` when `value->type == CborMapType`, otherwise `false`. Use it to verify a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR map before map-specific handling.
functions.cbor_value_get_tag: Returns the tag number from a `CborValue` that is already a tag. Use only after checking `cbor_value_is_tag(value)` (or when you know it’s a tag). On success, stores the tag in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`; otherwise the assert fires in debug builds.
functions.cbor_value_get_simple_type: Returns the CBOR “simple value” payload from a `CborValue`. Use only after `cbor_value_is_simple_type(value)` is true; it asserts otherwise. On success, stores `value->extra` in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_null: `cbor_encode_null()` writes the CBOR null simple value to the given `CborEncoder`. Use it when you want to encode a null item in a CBOR stream. It returns the result of `cbor_encode_simple_value()`, so it reports any encoding/error conditions from the encoder.
functions._cbor_value_begin_string_iteration: Starts string-chunk iteration. Set on a `CborValue` before reading chunks of a text/byte string. It marks “iterating” and “before first chunk”; for indefinite-length strings it advances to the first chunk. Always returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_is_text_string: Checks whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR text string. Use it to test the item type before reading/extracting text. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborTextStringType`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_text_string_chunk: Returns one chunk of a text string. Use only on a text-string `CborValue`; it asserts that type, then forwards to `_cbor_value_get_string_chunk`. On success it fills `bufferptr`, `len`, and `next` with the chunk data and next position.
functions.cbor_parser_init_reader: Initializes a parser for an external/streaming source via `ops` and `token`. Set `parser`, `it`, and mark the iterator as one remaining item, then preparse the first value. Use it when data isn’t in a flat buffer; it returns `preparse_value(it)`’s error/status.
functions.cbor_value_is_half_float: `cbor_value_is_half_float()` is a quick type check for a CBOR value. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborHalfFloatType`, i.e. the item is a half-precision float; otherwise `false`. Use it to test before reading the value.
functions.cbor_value_copy_byte_string: Copies the current CBOR byte string into `buffer` and returns its length in `*buflen`; `next` gets the position after it. Use only when `value` is a byte string. It asserts that in debug builds, then delegates to the generic string-copy helper.
functions.cbor_value_get_raw_integer: Returns the integer’s raw encoded value as `uint64_t`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true; it asserts that in debug builds. On success it stores the extracted value in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_get_type: Returns the current CBOR item type stored in `value->type`. Use it to inspect a `CborValue` before decoding/branching on its kind. It’s a direct accessor: no validation, no side effects, and it just returns the cached type.
functions.cbor_encode_uint: Encodes a CBOR unsigned integer into the given `CborEncoder`. Use it with a valid encoder and a `uint64_t` value. It returns the result of `encode_number`, so success/failure depends on the encoder state and available space.
functions.cbor_value_get_uint64: Returns the current CBOR item as an unsigned 64-bit integer. Use only when `cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer(value)` is true; it asserts otherwise. On success, writes the extracted value to `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_to_json_advance: Converts the current `CborValue` to JSON and advances it via `value_to_json`. Use with a valid `FILE*`, `CborValue*`, and flags. It returns a `CborError` from the conversion; recursion is capped by `CBOR_PARSER_MAX_RECURSIONS`.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_buffer_size: Returns how many bytes the encoder has written into `buffer` so far: `encoder->data.ptr - buffer`. Use it after encoding to get the used buffer size. It assumes `buffer` is the start of the same output buffer; otherwise the result is invalid.
functions.cbor_encoder_init:
Initializes a `CborEncoder` to write CBOR into `buffer` with capacity `size`. Set `flags` as needed. It stores start/end pointers and sets `remaining=2`; actual encoding then uses this state. If `buffer`/`size` are invalid, behavior follows normal pointer/bounds use.
Initialize the encoder with a real output buffer and only valid documented flags; never feed unvalidated user data directly into flags. For buffer-based encoding, prefer flags = 0 (or another explicitly documented safe combination). Ensure the encoder mode selected by flags matches the initialized internal state, so later calls such as cbor_encoder_create_map do not interpret a buffer pointer as a function pointer.
functions.cbor_encode_negative_int: Encodes a CBOR negative integer from its absolute value: it writes `-1 - absolute_value`. Use with the magnitude of the negative number, not the signed value. It delegates to `encode_number`; overflow/underflow handling depends on that helper.
functions.cbor_value_is_container: `cbor_value_is_container()` checks whether a `CborValue` is a container item: it returns true for arrays or maps, false otherwise. Use it to test an iterator/value before treating it as nested data.
functions.cbor_value_get_array_length: Gets an array’s definite length. Call only on array values; if length is unknown, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. On success writes `*length`. If the encoded size won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions._cbor_value_extract_int64_helper: Helper to read a `CborValue`’s integer payload. Use it only for integer values. It returns `value->extra` for normal-sized integers, and falls back to `_cbor_value_decode_int64_internal()` when `CborIteratorFlag_IntegerValueTooLarge` is set.
functions.cbor_parser_init: Initializes a `CborParser` and first `CborValue` for parsing a CBOR buffer. Pass the input bytes, size, flags, and output structs. It sets parser state, points `it` at `buffer`, then pre-parses the first value; returns that parse error/status.
functions.cbor_value_is_null: `cbor_value_is_null()` is a simple type check: it returns true only when `value->type == CborNullType`. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` represents CBOR `null`; it does not validate or inspect any other state.
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size: `_cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size()` is a thin helper for CBOR strings. It computes the current string chunk’s byte size via `get_string_chunk_size()`, ignoring the returned offset. Use it with a valid `CborValue*` and `size_t* len`; it returns a `CborError` and fills `len` on success.
functions.cbor_value_is_length_known: `cbor_value_is_length_known()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator points to a definite-length item. Use it before relying on `cbor_value_get_array_length()`/`_map_length()`. It returns `true` when the `UnknownLength` flag is not set, `false` for indefinite-length items.
functions.cbor_value_validate: Validates the CBOR item at `it` with `flags`. It copies the iterator, runs `validate_value(...)`, and returns that error if any. If `CborValidateCompleteData` is set, extra unread bytes cause `CborErrorGarbageAtEnd`; otherwise `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_begin_string_iteration: Starts chunked-string iteration for a text/byte string `CborValue`. Use only on string values and only once before iterating chunks. It asserts if the value isn’t a string or is already iterating; then delegates to the internal iterator setup.
functions.cbor_value_get_double: Returns the IEEE-754 double stored in a CBOR value. Use only when `cbor_value_is_double(value)` is true; it asserts that and that the encoded integer bits are present. It decodes the 64-bit payload and memcpy’s it into `*result`, then returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_at_end: `cbor_value_at_end()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator has no remaining items in the current container. Use it while iterating arrays/maps to stop at the end. It returns `true` when `it->remaining == 0`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_length: Returns the definite length of a byte/text string. Use only on string values; it asserts if not. If length is unknown (indefinite), returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. On success writes `*length`; if it won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions.cbor_encode_raw:
`cbor_encode_raw` appends `length` bytes from `raw` directly to the encoder buffer as raw data. Use it when you already have encoded bytes to insert. It returns the result of `append_to_buffer`, so it can fail if the buffer/encoder can’t accept the data.
Yes, this crash is caused by API misuse. Do not call cbor_encode_raw with a CborEncoder initialized using arbitrary or fuzzed flags. Initialize the encoder only with valid tinycbor-defined flags (typically 0, or documented constants only), and ensure the encoder remains in a valid state before encoding. Check the return value of cbor_encoder_init/cbor_encoder_create_array-related operations indirectly by validating setup assumptions, and stop encoding if earlier operations report errors. Also ensure the output buffer and length are consistent, and avoid reusing an encoder whose internal state may be invalid due to unsupported flag combinations.
functions.cbor_value_is_boolean: `cbor_value_is_boolean()` is a simple type check. Use it on a `CborValue*` to see whether the current CBOR item is a boolean. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborBooleanType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_tag: `cbor_encode_tag` writes a CBOR semantic tag to the output. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder` before encoding the tagged item. It does not change array/map element counts. It returns a `CborError` from the underlying number-encoding routine.
functions.cbor_value_enter_container:
Purpose: descend into a CBOR array/map and initialize `recursed` to iterate its contents. Use it on a container `CborValue`; it copies state, reads length, and sets remaining items. Unknown-length containers get `UINT32_MAX`. Errors: oversized length/map count => `CborErrorDataTooLarge`, with position reset to `it`.
Use cbor_value_enter_container() only when cbor_value_is_container() is true, then iterate the child CborValue until normal end-of-container before leaving. Treat the entered iterator as invalid for cbor_value_leave_container() if traversal terminated due to parse error rather than successful exhaustion.
functions.cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk: Returns one chunk of a byte string. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_byte_string(value)` is true. It fills `bufferptr`/`len` with the chunk data and `next` with the following `CborValue`; it delegates to the generic string-chunk helper.
functions.cbor_encode_double: `cbor_encode_double` writes a CBOR floating-point item as a 64-bit double. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and a `double` value. It just forwards to `cbor_encode_floating_point(..., CborDoubleType, &value)` and returns the resulting `CborError`.
functions.cbor_value_reparse: `cbor_value_reparse` refreshes an iterator’s current item metadata. If `IteratingStringChunks` is set, it does nothing and returns `CborNoError`; otherwise it reparses the current value via `preparse_next_value_nodecrement(it)`. Use it after the underlying data may have changed.
functions.cbor_value_to_json: `cbor_value_to_json` is a convenience wrapper that prints a CBOR value as JSON to `out` without advancing the caller’s `CborValue`. It copies `*value` locally, then calls `cbor_value_to_json_advance`. Use it when you want JSON output and don’t need iterator state changed.
functions.cbor_value_is_tag: `cbor_value_is_tag()` is a simple type check. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR tag item before reading it as a tag. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborTagType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_negative_integer: `cbor_value_is_negative_integer()` checks whether a `CborValue` is an integer encoded as CBOR negative integer. Use it on a parsed value before reading it as signed/negative. It returns true only if the value is integer and has the negative-integer flag; otherwise false.
functions.cbor_value_get_boolean: Returns a CBOR boolean’s native `bool` value. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_boolean(value)`; it asserts otherwise. On success, stores `true`/`false` in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions._cbor_value_finish_string_iteration: Finishes iterating a CBOR string/byte string. If the string is indefinite-length, it skips the Break byte; then it advances to the next item via `preparse_next_value()`. Use it after consuming all chunks of a string.
functions.cbor_value_is_double: `cbor_value_is_double` checks whether a `CborValue` currently holds a CBOR double (floating-point) value. Use it to test the type before reading it as a double. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborDoubleType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_float: `cbor_encode_float` writes a CBOR float value from a `float` into the given `CborEncoder`. Use it when encoding a 32-bit floating-point number. It returns the result of `cbor_encode_floating_point`; on success it emits the float, otherwise it reports the encoding error.
functions.cbor_value_copy_text_string: Copies a CBOR text string into a caller buffer. Use only on a text-string `CborValue`; `buffer`/`buflen` hold output capacity/size. On success it copies data and, if `next` is non-NULL, returns the next item. It asserts if `value` isn’t text.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags: `cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags` is a convenience wrapper to pretty-print a `CborValue` to a `FILE*` with formatting flags, advancing `*value` as it prints. Use it when you want stream output via `FILE*`; it returns the underlying `CborError` from `cbor_value_to_pretty_stream`.
functions._cbor_value_decode_int64_internal:
Decodes the stored integer payload from a `CborValue` that was already identified as too large for normal integer handling or as float/double. Use only internally after those checks. If `IntegerValueIs64Bit` is set, it reads 64 bits; otherwise 32 bits.
Misuse: this is an internal helper that assumes CborValue was produced by tinycbor's parser and that all iterator invariants hold, including valid type/flags and sufficient backing bytes. Do not call or reach it with a manually fabricated CborValue. Create the iterator via cbor_parser_init() and parser traversal APIs, and only decode values that the parser identified as present and complete within the input buffer.
functions.cbor_value_is_byte_string: `cbor_value_is_byte_string()` is a simple type check. Use it on a `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is a CBOR byte string. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborByteStringType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_integer: `cbor_value_is_integer()` is a simple type check: it returns true iff `value->type == CborIntegerType`. Use it to test a `CborValue` before reading it as an integer. It does no conversion or validation beyond the stored type.
functions._cbor_value_dup_string: Allocates and copies a CBOR string into a new NUL-terminated buffer. Call with `buffer`/`buflen` set; on success `*buffer` points to malloc’d data, `*buflen` is length+1, and `next` advances past the string. Returns OOM or copy/parse errors.
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float: Returns the decoded half-float payload from a `CborValue` into `result`. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_half_float(value)`. It asserts on wrong type or oversized integer state; otherwise it copies `value->extra` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end: Checks whether a string iterator has reached the last chunk/end. Use on a `CborValue` while iterating string chunks. It returns `true` when `cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size()` reports `CborErrorNoMoreStringChunks`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_int: Encodes a signed 64-bit integer as CBOR. Pass an initialized `CborEncoder*` and the `int64_t` value. It maps nonnegative values to unsigned integers and negative values to CBOR negative integers, then delegates to `encode_number`; errors come from that helper.
functions.cbor_value_validate_basic: `cbor_value_validate_basic` is a lightweight sanity check for a `CborValue`. It copies the iterator and calls `cbor_value_advance`, so it validates that the current item can be advanced past without modifying the original. It returns the advance error code.
functions.cbor_value_is_float: `cbor_value_is_float` checks whether a `CborValue` currently holds a CBOR float. Use it to test the value’s type before reading it as a floating-point number. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborFloatType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64: Returns the current CBOR integer as `int64_t`. Use it only on integer values (`cbor_value_is_integer(value)`), or the assert may fire. It writes the decoded result to `*result`; negative CBOR integers are converted via `-n-1`. Always returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_byte_string: Encodes a CBOR byte string (major type 2) into `encoder` from `string` with exact `length`. Use it for raw bytes, not text. It returns `encode_string(...)`’s status: success on valid input/space, otherwise an error from the encoder.
functions.cbor_value_is_array: `cbor_value_is_array()` is a simple type check for a `CborValue`. Use it to test whether the current value is an array before treating it as one. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborArrayType`, otherwise `false`.
